summary: The note describes how local musicians in Milltown have embraced technology since September 2023, from home studios and software synthesis to blockchain distribution, projection-mapped live shows, field-recording sound design, online communities and updated music education. It also covers challenges such as market saturation, electronic waste and questions of authenticity, concluding that technology is a tool while the soul of the music stays with the creator.
one_line: Milltown's local musicians use home studios, software synths, blockchain distribution and immersive live visuals to innovate, while facing saturation, e-waste and authenticity concerns.
key_facts: Tommy Evers and Sara Liang turned small apartments in Milltown into professional-grade recording studios using laptops, DAWs and plugins since the latter part of 2023.
Tommy Evers said, "Gone are the days when you needed a label and a recording contract to get your music polished and heard."
Software mentioned for production includes Ableton Live and Logic Pro X, and for synthesis Serum and Omnisphere.
Sara Liang has been a classical pianist since the age of five and said the leap from a grand piano to a MIDI controller was daunting at first.
On October 15, 2023, The Melodic Collective, a local consortium of independent artists, launched a blockchain-based platform to distribute music directly to listeners.
Pauline Gomes, a DJ and producer who helped spearhead the blockchain initiative, said it allows transparent, peer-to-peer transactions and cuts out the middleman.

Electro-pop duo Neon Dreams use projection mapping and interactive visuals that respond to the music and audience movement; after a November 10, 2023 show they explained they synchronised MIDI controllers with visual software.
Sound designer Alex Torres turns field recordings of city life and a local park into rhythms and harmonies using SpectraLayers and GRM Tools.
The online forum "Milltown Soundscapes" was created in September 2023 for musicians, producers and enthusiasts to exchange tips and collaborate.
Ivy Winters, professor of music technology at Milltown University since September 2023, updated the curriculum to include AI-generated music and advanced sound design.
Challenges named include market saturation from easy access to production software, electronic waste from obsolete gear, and critics questioning the 'humanness' of digital music.
